before_behavior: Executor works through the wave plan wave by wave: checkpoint, Guard, implement, Verify. After the final wave, it writes execution-receipt.json and signals Archive. The SKILL.md describes no check on the built module's acceptance test file — execution-receipt.json is written when all waves pass Verifier, regardless of whether tests/acceptance.md exists for the module that was built.
after_behavior: When the task-card declares task_type as module-build, executor adds a post-final-wave check before writing execution-receipt.json: it reads the task-card to identify the target module and checks for tests/acceptance.md at modules/{layer}/{module}/tests/acceptance.md. If the file is absent, executor emits ACCEPTANCE_NOT_COVERED (error type SPEC_VIOLATION, which routes to loop_back per the error routing table) and does not write the execution receipt. The session loops back to acceptance test authorship before the task is declared complete.

benchmark_gates.rationale: A module-build task completed without tests/acceptance.md is a missed test gate — the module enters the corpus without a defined acceptance standard. The target is 0.0 because acceptance files are already required by the framework for all 99 registered modules; any module-build task completing without one is a protocol violation, not an edge case. One ACCEPTANCE_NOT_COVERED miss allowed is one module that can never be formally verified.
